column1: # Linux kernel local privilege-escalation CVEs, matched automatically by the kernel detector
# against the running version. min/max is an INCLUSIVE mainline range.
# IMPORTANT: these are mainline ranges. Every distribution backports fixes into older version
# numbers, so a kernel whose number sits in a range is a LEAD, not proof - confirm against the
# exact package build (and, where noted, the distro) before relying on an exploit. That caution
# is exactly what a learner should internalise, which is why every row repeats it in miniature.
# min       max        cve             name                    severity  description

column6: Copy-on-write race: any local user writes to read-only memory and overwrites a root-owned file or SUID binary. Extremely reliable public exploits. Fixed builds share the same version numbers, so confirm the patch level.
A pipe-buffer flag leak lets any local user overwrite read-only files (e.g. /etc/passwd, a SUID binary) and get root. One-shot and very reliable. Fixed in 5.16.11 / 5.15.25 / 5.10.102.
Heap out-of-bounds write in netfilter, reachable from an unprivileged user namespace on distros that enable them - local root.
Ubuntu overlayfs lets an unprivileged user create files as root via a user-namespace mount. Ubuntu-specific.
eBPF verifier sign-extension flaw gives arbitrary kernel read/write when unprivileged BPF is allowed (kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=0).
eBPF verifier 32-bit bounds bug - kernel read/write and root when unprivileged BPF is enabled.
Netfilter nf_tables use-after-free reachable from an unprivileged user namespace - local root on many recent distros.
Route filter double-free, weaponised with the DirtyCred technique for local root across a wide kernel range.
/proc/pid/mem write validation bug - a classic one-shot local root on older kernels.
Another nf_tables use-after-free giving local root from a user namespace; distro exploits published.
